rubric.long_description: An arguable claim that the essay supports throughout.

submission.body:
The Case for Later School Start Times

Teenagers are not lazy; they are biologically out of sync with a 7:30 AM bell. When Seattle moved high school start times to 8:45, students slept a median of 34 minutes more and their grades rose.

Critics point to bus costs and after-school jobs. Those costs are real, but they are smaller than the cost of a generation that learns while exhausted.

bodies.name: Lab Report: Osmosis
bodies.description:
Write up the potato-core osmosis lab using the lab guide. Include your data table and one graph of mass change against sucrose concentration.

Checklist

  • Hypothesis and method
  • Data table with units
  • Graph with error bars
  • Discussion of at least two sources of error

Upload a PDF or Word document. You get two attempts; the second one counts.

rubric.long_description: States a testable hypothesis and describes the procedure clearly enough to repeat.
Tables and graphs are labeled, with units and error bars.
Explains the results using membrane transport concepts and names sources of error.

bodies.body: Answers attached in order: 1) 4/3, 2) π, 3) 0, 4) 12, 5) 1/2.

The Case for Later School Start Times

Teenagers are not lazy; they are biologically out of sync with a 7:30 AM bell. When Seattle moved high school start times to 8:45, students slept a median of 34 minutes more and their grades rose.

Critics point to bus costs and after-school jobs. Those costs are real, but they are smaller than the cost of a generation that learns while exhausted.

submission_history.body:
The Case for Later School Start Times

Teenagers are not lazy; they are biologically out of sync with a 7:30 AM bell. Districts that moved start times past 8:30 saw attendance and grades rise.
